esm.note: no tag at this commit; the commit is the pin. pyproject declares transformers @ main (floating): install the transformers pin first, then esm with --no-deps

transformers.origin: the Biohub fork of transformers; the Biohub/transformers repository is no longer public, and github.com/huggingface/transformers serves the same commit unchanged

archive_recipe: git archive --format=tar --prefix=<name>-<commit8>/ <commit> <paths> | gzip -n -9  (esm: esm pyproject.toml LICENSE.md THIRD_PARTY_NOTICE.md; transformers: src/transformers setup.py pyproject.toml LICENSE README.md)

pinned_stack.tested_on: H100 80GB HBM3 (sm_90) on the pinned stack (python 3.12.10 / torch 2.13.0+cu130 / triton 3.7.1 / flash_attn 2.8.3.post1 / xformers 0.0.35+03b91d7.d20260904 / transformer_engine 2.15.0+42b8400): the freeze plus the "image" layer below — a documentation line, compared against by nothing (check_pins.py pins the installed distributions, esmfold2_opt/attn.py the live kernel paths)
pinned_stack.note: the stack = environment/requirements.lock: every distribution of the tested environment, the accelerated layer included ("image": flash-attn, xformers, transformer-engine and transformer-engine's pinned pure-Python dependencies — the three extension wheels install from stock/wheels/, every other line from the index or git)

torch_build.source: PyPI default wheel (CUDA 13.0 build; nvidia-*-cu13 runtime wheels per the freeze)

image.base: the accelerated layer = an environment holding the kit's freeze (python 3.12.10, torch 2.13.0+cu130, triton 3.7.1, the CUDA 13.0 runtime wheels, both pinned forks installed at their pinned commits) plus the environment variables of "env" and ONE install step: the three wheels below (flash-attn, xformers, transformer-engine — Biohub's fastest documented environment for this model), each checked against its sha256 then installed --no-deps --no-index, then transformer-engine's pure-Python runtime dependencies at the exact versions of "python_deps" (--no-deps; every one a new install, nothing of the freeze up- or downgraded: the pip-freeze difference is these additions only). Without the layer upstream's FLASH_ATTN_AVAILABLE / _te_available are False, the atom transformers run SDPA and the LM the pure-PyTorch LayerNorm+MLP — stock/check_pins.py refuses it by name
image.layer: sha256sum -c <the three wheels' lines> && python -m pip install --no-deps --no-index <flash-attn whl> <xformers whl> <transformer-engine whl> && python -m pip install --no-deps <python_deps, pinned ==>

wheels.name: flash_attn-2.8.3.post1-cp312-cp312-linux_x86_64.whl

wheels.build: on the base image (its python 3.12.10 / torch 2.13.0+cu130 / gcc 12.2.0, cxx11 ABI), nvcc 13.0.88 from NVIDIA's debian12 apt repository (cuda-compiler-13-0 cuda-libraries-dev-13-0 cuda-cudart-dev-13-0 cuda-profiler-api-13-0; build box only, not in the image), ninja 1.13.0, FLASH_ATTN_CUDA_ARCHS=90 TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST=9.0 MAX_JOBS=40 NVCC_THREADS=1 FLASH_ATTENTION_FORCE_BUILD=TRUE: python -m pip wheel --no-build-isolation --no-deps flash_attn-2.8.3.post1.tar.gz

image.note: sm_90 cubins only (H100 / H200, the target hardware): on another architecture the packages import, upstream takes its accelerated branches and the first kernel launch raises (no kernel image) — loud, never a silent slow run. Observed in the image on a CPU box: flash_attn, xformers.ops, transformer_engine.pytorch, flash_attn.ops.triton.rotary import; FLASH_ATTN_AVAILABLE and _te_available / _xformers_available True; pip check clean

a100.for: compute capability 8.0 (A100 80GB): the same base, the same "env", the same "layer" step and "python_deps", with the three wheels below in place of "image".wheels — the SAME sources and versions ("python_packages" unchanged, so stock/check_pins.py judges both images alike) compiled for sm_80 and sm_90 (FLASH_ATTN_CUDA_ARCHS / NVTE_CUDA_ARCHS "80;90", TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST "8.0;9.0"); the freezes of the two images differ only in these three wheels' file lines
a100.tested_on: A100-SXM4-80GB and A100 80GB PCIe (an image assembled by exactly this recipe): flash_attn_func / xformers memory_efficient_attention / te.LayerNormMLP launch on sm_80 and agree with SDPA / plain LayerNorm+MLP math (max |d| 2.1e-3 / 1.7e-3 / rel 4.3e-3, run-to-run equal); upstream's FLASH_ATTN_AVAILABLE, TE_AVAILABLE, TRITON_KERNELS_AVAILABLE True; check_pins clean
a100.configuration: configs/a100.env (MODEL_OPT_TARGET_GPU=A100; every other line as configs/h100.env)

full_freeze: environment/requirements.lock (128 lines: every distribution of the tested environment, read back from it with pip freeze --all)

system.compiler: gcc/cc + Python headers required at run time (Triton JIT)
system.accelerated: flash_attn 2.8.3.post1, xformers 0.0.35, transformer_engine 2.15.0 — the pinned image's one layer ("image"): upstream's modeling_esmfold2_common.FLASH_ATTN_AVAILABLE is True (the atom transformers run flash_attn_varlen_func), modeling_esmc._te_available is True (the LM binds te.LayerNormMLP / LayerNormLinear / Linear) and its rotary runs flash-attn's Triton kernel; xformers is importable and unreachable from ESMFold2 (the LM attention stays F.scaled_dot_product_attention with the chain-aware mask). The package prints atom_attn / esmc_mlp / esmc_attn / esmc_rope on every route (opt/esmfold2_opt/attn.py) and ESMFOLD2_OPT_REQUIRE_FAST_ENV=1 (configs/h100.env) refuses a box where a required one is not live

entry_point.fold: esm.models.esmfold2.ESMFold2InputBuilder().fold(model, StructurePredictionInput(...), num_loops=, num_sampling_steps=, num_diffusion_samples=, seed=, msa_max_depth=, lm_dropout=, msa_column_mask_rate=, complex_id=)
entry_point.msa_input: esm.utils.msa.MSA.from_a3m(path, remove_insertions=, max_sequences=) attached as ProteinInput(msa=...)
entry_point.result: MolecularComplexResult(complex, plddt, ptm, iptm, pae, pde, distogram, pair_chains_iptm, ...); structure file = result.complex.to_mmcif()
entry_point.script: opt/esmfold2_opt/stock_fold.py (the tree's one stock caller: the calls above plus the settings preset's two model calls set_kernel_backend / set_chunk_size, nothing else on the path; settings presets: opt/esmfold2_opt/settings.py SETTINGS_PRESETS)

model.note: kernel_backend / chunk_size: the model's own state after from_pretrained (the reference kernel path, pair-block chunk 64); the fold() keywords above override the config values at call time

library_defaults.precision: PyTorch defaults (matmul TF32 off, float32_matmul_precision highest, cudnn TF32 on)

msa_read.note: esm.utils.msa.MSA.from_a3m keyword defaults (insertions kept, the whole file read)

config_class_defaults.note: the transformers ESMFold2 config CLASS defaults (configuration_esmfold2.py:251, :138, :252, :137), not what the shipped checkpoints carry (see config_json_shipped)

config_json_shipped.note: what the checkpoints' own config.json files carry (the same keys and values in both; byte-identical across the HF revisions read, including the snapshots pinned under "weights"); fold() keyword arguments (num_loops=, num_sampling_steps=, num_diffusion_samples=, lm_dropout=) override them at call time, so every settings preset states them explicitly

executed_steps.note: denoising steps executed for num_sampling_steps=N: sample() truncates the N-entry schedule at max_inference_sigma=256 (modeling_esmfold2_common.py:1788, :1809-1818) with the checkpoint's schedule constants above; recorded, not computed

variants.note: every variant loads biohub/ESMC-6B as the language model (from_pretrained load_esmc=True); one variant per process
